close_reason: Positive observation, no action required. The validate-and-collect destroy loop at metadata.rs:470-481 encodes the validated invariant in the type system (Vec<String>, not Vec<Value>) — removes the 'unreachable' dead branch that the original two-pass design had. Closing as 'noted, what good looks like'.
description:
Why this is good: bbde4c3 refactored the destroy loop from a two-pass validation (find() pre-check + match in loop with 'unreachable' arm) to a single pass that walks destroy_arr once, pushing String to id_strs on Some, returning invalidArguments on None. The validated invariant is now ENCODED in the type — the loop processes Vec<String>, not Vec<Value> — instead of in a comment-as-assertion.

The original code had a None arm carrying 'continue, // unreachable' which is exactly the kind of dead branch that gets converted into a real bug by a future refactor removing the pre-check. The current code cannot suffer that fate: there is no second pass, no dead branch.

The commit message (bbde4c3) explicitly calls out 'The dead branch was a future-bug magnet'.

A future contributor might suggest 'fold the two loops back together for symmetry with create/update' (which use a single map iteration). Defend: the destroy phase has a fundamentally different validation surface (a flat array, not a map). The current split is type-driven, not stylistic.

Cross-reference: bd:JMAP-ayoz.30.
title: validate-and-collect destroy loop (metadata.rs:470-481) — invariant moved into the type system instead of a comment
